correctness.rationale: Graph diameter≤2 follows from Δ(H)<n/2. Strictly convex variance on anchored Lipschitz polytope forces connected tight-edge spanning graph at a maximizing vertex and integral 0/1/2 values. Opposite levels A,B form an H-biclique and have exact n² variance numerator n(a+b)−(a−b)². For ab≤k≤(n−2)/2, t=a+b≤ab+1≤n/2 and monotonicity proves star envelope and unique strict extremizers. For a,b≤r<n/2, equality at a=b=r forces an isolated H-Krr component. Floor threshold and n=4 boundary hold. Independent exact enumeration and symbolic/integer checks corroborate all formulas; proof is all n.

value.rationale: Sharp resilience budgets explain how many arbitrary missing edges or missing neighbors a complete graph tolerates before its Lipschitz variance can increase, with extremal star versus balanced biclique geometry. Two different natural perturbation norms, exact transition and rigidity make this a meaningful infinite-graph-family classification.

limitations: Connected unweighted simple graphs, uniform vertex probabilities, n≥4; edge budget k≤floor((n−2)/2), degree budget r<n/2; no larger budgets or weighted metrics.
